name: Saint George
history: A soldier martyred at Lydda in Palestine, probably under Diocletian, and venerated across East and West from the earliest centuries. The story of the dragon came much later and is legend. Crusaders brought his cult home, Edward III placed the Order of the Garter under his protection, and he became the patron saint of England.
life: Almost nothing is known for certain of George’s life. His tomb at Lydda, the modern Lod, was a place of pilgrimage by the sixth century, and churches were dedicated to him throughout the Christian East. Pope Gelasius in 494 counted him among those whose names are rightly honoured but whose deeds are known only to God. The legend of the dragon, slain to save a princess and a town that then accepted baptism, was spread through the West by the Golden Legend in the thirteenth century. English devotion grew with the Crusades; his feast was kept in England from 1222, Edward III founded the Order of the Garter in his honour around 1348, and his red cross became the national flag. He is also a patron of soldiers, scouts, Georgia, Catalonia and Portugal, and Eastern Christians call him the Great Martyr.
prayerTo: Saint George, soldier of Christ, you gave up rank and life rather than deny your Lord. Pray for England, for soldiers and all who serve and protect others, and for me, that I may fight the dragons of my own sins with courage and trust in the grace of God. Amen.
penance: Pray today for England and for those who serve in the armed forces. Choose one fault you have been tolerating and take it on with a small, definite act.
meditation: The dragon is legend; the courage is not. What is the dragon in your own life that you have been afraid to face?
